source.title: Open problems in combinatorial group theory

accepted.question_text: The Andrews-Curtis conjecture asks whether, for the free group F = F_n of finite rank n ≥ 2 with fixed free generators X = {x1, ..., xn}, every set Y = {y1, ..., yn} of elements of F that generates F as a normal subgroup is Andrews-Curtis equivalent to X, meaning that one can get from X to Y by a sequence of Nielsen transformations together with conjugations by elements of F.

evidence.quote: The Andrews-Curtis conjecture asks whether, for the free group F = F_n of finite rank n ≥ 2 with fixed free generators X = {x1, ..., xn}, every set Y = {y1, ..., yn} of elements of F that generates F as a normal subgroup is Andrews-Curtis equivalent to X, meaning that one can get from X to Y by a sequence of Nielsen transformations together with conjugations by elements of F.

accepted.question_text: Let Epi(n, k) be the set of all homomorphisms from a free group F_n onto a free group F_k, where n, k ≥ 2. Do there exist two elements g1, g2 ∈ F_n such that whenever φ(g_i) = ψ(g_i) for i = 1, 2 and φ, ψ ∈ Epi(n, k), one must have φ = ψ? In other words, is every homomorphism in Epi(n, k) completely determined by its values on just two elements?

evidence.quote: Let Epi(n, k) be the set of all homomorphisms from a free group F_n onto a free group F_k, where n, k ≥ 2.
